doc_name: List of speakers of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly
text: The Speaker is the presiding officer of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, the primary law-making body for the Indian state of Tamil Nadu, and is elected by the members of the assembly from among them. The Madras Legislative Council, the first representative legislature for the Madras Presidency, was established in December 1920, with P. Rajagopalachari nominated as its first president, who took office on 17 December 1920. The Government of India Act 1935 introduced provincial autonomy in 1937, transforming the Madras Legislative Council into the upper chamber of a bicameral legislature, with its presiding officer thereafter known as the chairman of the council. This structure continued until the council was abolished in 1986, following Indian Independence. In 1937, the Madras Legislative Assembly was also established as part of this bicameral system, with its presiding officer designated as the speaker. Madras State, which served as the precursor to the current state of Tamil Nadu, was formed after India became a republic on 26 January 1950 and included present-day Tamil Nadu along with parts of present-day Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Kerala. The first legislature of Madras State elected on the basis of universal suffrage was constituted on 1 March 1952, following general elections held in January 1952. Madras State was officially renamed Tamil Nadu in January 1969.
